Structural session dropped _exeque from floor 15 to 12: pre-computing a pointer to D_8009BE7C closed the final-callback block byte-exact; the triple-store residual survives two more reordering probes

Floor held at 12/187; exhausted pure-C respelling of the triple-store block (5 measured spellings, all byte-identical) and traced the exact rank_for_schedule LUID tie with the instrumented cc1's BB2_R
Directed permuter campaigns dropped _exeque's honest floor 12 -> 2/187 via two SOTN-sanctioned do-while(0) wraps (single-level around the triple-store block, then nested around its first two stores);

frontier.hypothesis: The floor-2 residual (final-callback jalr delay-slot fill) is the SAME site s2's H6 found closable only via `volatile s32 *p` -- an IRQ-callback-installed function's own single-read test-and-clear of a flag it owns could qualify as a fourth catalogued use-site shape under legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched, closing the last 2 instructions with zero further search once ruled on.
frontier.mechanism: policy/ruling question, not a GCC pass
frontier.next_probe: File a ruling-request citing memory/grind/_exeque/rejected/volatile-D_8009BE7C-guard-clear.c, hypotheses.md H6, src/display.c's DMACallback(2, _exeque); IRQ-install site, and this session's confirmation that the floor is now ONLY 2/187 (down from 12), all concentrated at this single site.

frontier.hypothesis: A non-volatile pure-C lever for the jalr-delay-slot fill may still exist outside plain-C statement reordering (e.g. a restructuring of the guard-and-clear block's control flow, or a different placement of the pointer/dereference relative to the call) that this session's single directed permuter campaign (9096 iterations, one chassis) did not surface.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 reorg.c fill_simple_delay_slots (excludes volatile-marked memory from delay-slot motion candidacy) -- the question is whether some OTHER C restructuring (not volatile) can independently make the store ineligible for delay-slot motion
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/reorg.c's fill_simple_delay_slots and its callers to see what OTHER conditions (besides MEM_VOLATILE_P) block a candidate insn from filling a jalr's delay slot; try a restructuring that trips one of those conditions without volatile.

frontier.hypothesis: The do-while(0) wraps banked this session (candidate.c) are a stable improved chassis for any future session on this function -- re-deriving them from scratch would waste a session.
frontier.next_probe: Next session should apply memory/grind/_exeque/candidate.c verbatim as its starting point (sandbox floor 2/187, confirmed this session) before attempting any new lever.
